Cross-Language Census: Python (CPython) net Standard Library × sa_std Gaps

This page is a member of the “cross-language std census batch” (same batch: Rust full std, Go net, Java net, .NET net, Android net, iOS net, the Unreal networking system; consistent methodology, and the SA-side baseline uniformly sci main 8a943911's sa_std). This page covers the Python (CPython) net standard library: with the public surface of the Lib layer in the latest stable CPython source on one side and the sa_std network surface on the other, it mechanically extracts the two-side inventories and compares them cluster by cluster, giving the four gap categories (existing equivalent / directly mappable / needs modeling / model mismatch) and a priority shortlist for closing gaps. For the Rust-side conclusions, see the Rust std Census page; the pages of the other lines are cross-linked when the main session integrates them.

Sources and Method

ItemContent
Python-side sourceCPython v3.15.0 (tag commit d220409a13b77de7a6c30abe16ea90db01528edc), shallow clone + blob filter + sparse checkout, taking only the network-related parts of Lib/ and Modules/ (working tree about 3 MB)
SA-side baselineThe sa_std/ network family files of sci main 8a943911 (the .sai/.sa/.sal/.sla of net/netx/http2/http_client/http_server/multipart/tls_client/tls_server/dtls/quic/ws_client/ssh and plugin_http_*, plugin_async) + the network-prefixed C functions of src/runtime/sa_std.h
Extraction methodPython side: AST extraction of module-level functions/classes and public methods/enum members/module-level constants (script tools/python_net_census/extract_python_surface.py); C-implemented modules (_socket/_ssl) follow the census methodology and take the Lib layer (socket.py/ssl.py) as authoritative, supplemented by scanning the C source with the PyMethodDef tables and constant registration macros for extra rows (sources marked separately in the inventory). SA side: extraction by the rules of @extern in .sai, #def in .sal, [MACRO] in .sa/.sal, and fn in .sla (script tools/python_net_census/extract_sa_surface.py). The two-side inventories (TSV) and the classification mapping table (python_net_gaps.tsv) are checked in with this page; the scripts are re-runnable
Comparison granularityClassification is in units of “capability clusters” (the functions/methods/constant groups of the same capability are normalized into one cluster), 78 clusters in total; the item-by-item correspondences within clusters are in the checked-in mapping table. Counts come only from the actually extracted inventories; surfaces that could not be extracted are noted honestly in “Coverage Boundaries” at the end

How to read this: sa_std's network main body (TCP/UDP/Unix/TLS/HTTP client and server/WebSocket/HTTP2 tool surface) corresponds to Python's mostly as “existing equivalent”; the gaps are concentrated in three places — TLS's configuration and certificate surface (the ssl cluster has 6 directly mappable + 3 needing modeling), the Web periphery tool surface (URL tools, Cookies, HTTP constants, authentication/proxy), and asyncio/socketserver's framework models (callback and handler models, mostly needs modeling or model mismatch — model differences, not capability absences).

The asyncio Network Surface (Separate Section)

asyncio's network surface is viewed in three layers: the coroutine-style connection/server layer and loop.sock_*, which SA corresponds to with the async fn + future/task coroutine surface, non-blocking handles and the netx io_uring reactor — existing equivalent; StreamReader/StreamWriter's buffered stream reader/writer (line reading, readuntil, drain flow control), for which SA has no corresponding surface yet — needs modeling; and the Transport/Protocol callback interface family, which is asyncio's root model and differs from SA's coroutine + explicit handle model — model mismatch. This matches the characterization of async runtimes in the Rust census of the same batch: the capability is reachable, the model is not ported.

Protocol Clients (Registration Style)

Python's protocol clients are all “text protocol helpers over TCP (+TLS)”; the SA side currently has only the raw connection surface and no protocol helpers at all. By real usage frequency only SMTP enters the priority shortlist; the rest are registered pending demand. nntplib has been removed upstream (PEP 594, removed in 3.13); the 3.15 source tree was measured to have no Lib/nntplib.py — not a gap, but an upstream extinction, registered for reference. Likewise, http.server's CGI handler and socketserver's ForkingMixIn have also been removed upstream (measured absent in the 3.15 tree).

Priority Shortlist for Closing Gaps

  1. Generic setsockopt/getsockopt pass-through (the socket escape hatch): a single pair of pass-through functions for arbitrary level/optname/byte values can backstop all unnamed options — the highest value-for-effort fill-in on the socket surface.
  2. The TLS configuration surface (an SSLContext equivalent): model SNI, verification modes/flags, ALPN, TLS version bounds, cipher lists, and in-memory certificate/CA loading with a ctx handle. The current sa_std_tls_client_connect has only (host, port); this is the largest contract gap between CXU/relay-style real usage surfaces and Python ssl.
  3. The peer certificate surface: a getpeercert equivalent (certificate chain + decoded fields) and standalone fetching (get_server_certificate), landing together with item 2.
  4. URL tool completion: quote/unquote/quote_plus/unquote_plus, parse_qs/parse_qsl, urlencode, urljoin — pure functions, low cost, filling in urllib.parse's high-frequency surface (currently only sa_std_url_parse basic splitting).
  5. HTTP status code/method named constants (the HTTPStatus/HTTPMethod equivalent surface): same family as the AJ census's registration of “http methods are only four kinds, status codes on the SLA surface”, filled in at once.
  6. The Cookie surface: http.cookies parsing/serialization + CookieJar policies and Netscape format persistence — a real Web client usage surface; SA currently has only raw header reading/writing.
  7. DNS small-item completion: getservbyname/getservbyport, getprotobyname/getprotobynumber, getfqdn, the if_nameindex family — a small and complete group.
  8. TLS upgrade of an existing connection (a start_tls equivalent): a prerequisite capability shared by asyncio and STARTTLS-style protocols (including the SMTP item).
  9. An ipaddress value type library (SLA layer): network/interface object operations (subnets/supernet/hosts/ overlaps/summarize/collapse) + address classification predicates — pure value semantics, best filled in as an SLA library, not via externs.
  10. An SMTP client helper: the only high-frequency item among protocol clients (including STARTTLS, depending on item 8); FTP/IMAP/POP3 are registered pending demand and do not enter the shortlist.

Coverage Boundaries and Unverified Surfaces

  • C-implemented modules take the Lib layer as authoritative (the unified census methodology): the main body of the socket class's methods is on _socket's C types; this page supplemented them by scanning the PyMethodDef tables, obtaining 42 methods counted as supplementary rows; _ssl's method tables are generated by Argument Clinic and the table scan did not cover them, so SSLContext's C method surface (load_cert_chain etc.) was not counted item by item — ssl's classification is based on ssl.py's visible surface + capability clusters, and that cluster's count is a lower bound.
  • socket's 608 constants are a source-registration upper bound: they include #ifdef platform-conditional names, and the number actually visible at runtime on a single platform is smaller; the SA side's 142 constants in net.sal are error codes + a family/type subset. Also note the existing registration: .sal's SA_NET_AF_IPV4/IPV6 are std-internal numbers and are not the same number system as the OS values returned by sa_net_addr_family (already registered by the AJ census, pending adjudication).
  • Inheritance not expanded: the methods carried by ipaddress's private base classes were measured at another 25 (_BaseNetwork 22 + _IPAddressBase 3), already counted in the capability judgments, but the 1163 extracted rows count only the concrete classes' own methods (44); cross-module inheritance (such as http.server handlers inheriting socketserver's BaseRequestHandler) was not expanded or deduplicated.
  • Token fallback extraction: http.server and http.cookies, because of CPython 3.15's new syntax (lazy import) exceeding the AST syntax surface of the box's Python 3.13, were handled by a token-stream extractor fallback; validated on 4 AST-parseable modules — ipaddress and urllib.parse agree item by item, while socket (+4 methods +4 functions) and ssl (+7 methods) are slightly more inclusive due to conditional/platform definitions, and the fallback counts take the inclusive methodology.
  • Out of scope: asyncio takes only network-related files; the loop's task management/timers and other non-network methods are not in the comparison; the SA side counts only the net family files and sa_std.h's network prefix, and supporting surfaces such as io/fs are not counted in the equivalence base (except where noted in the text); whether http_client's HTTPS is built in at the implementation layer is not within the contract-layer evidence, and this page judges only the contract surface.
